title: kanban-tdd workflow configuration
description:
Binds the kanban-tdd plugin to one repository's board, branches and test commands. The skills themselves are repo-agnostic; everything that varies between projects lives here.

Deliberately absent: the repository owner and name. Those come from `git remote`, so a fork, a rename or a transfer cannot leave a stale value here.

project.description: The GitHub Projects v2 board this repo's work is tracked on.

owner.description: User or organisation login that owns the board. Not necessarily the repo owner — one board often spans several repos.

ownerType.description: Decides whether gh is called with --owner @me / a login, and which GraphQL root is used.

number.description: The board number, from its URL: /users/<owner>/projects/<number>.

url.description: Human-readable link, for messages and ticket bodies.

statusField.description: Name of the single-select field holding the column. GitHub's templates call it Status; a custom board may not.

columns.description:
Maps the workflow's internal phase names to the literal option names on the board. Matched EXACTLY, case included. `ghboard validate` reads the live options and fails if a configured column is missing, rather than silently creating a duplicate.

Four are required: backlog, ready, inProgress, done. Everything between inProgress and done depends on how many environments you promote through. A two-branch project uses `inReview`. A project that opens a PR per environment uses `pushedToDev`, `pushedToStaging` and `readyForProd` instead, or alongside. Declare only the ones your board has.

backlog.description: Written but not approved to start.

inProgress.description: A feature branch exists and red→green is under way. Also where a card returns when human verification fails.

inReview.description: Merged to the integration branch and awaiting human verification. The simple case: one integration environment, one review gate. Omit it if you use the pushedTo* trio.

done.description: Verified by a human. Moving a card here is what authorises a release.

pushedToDev.description: Optional. Merged to the integration branch and deployed to a dev environment. Set by review-handoff.

pushedToStaging.description: Optional. Promoted from integration to staging. Set by release-to-production on the first promotion.

readyForProd.description: Optional, and the most valuable of the three. A HUMAN moves a card here after testing it on staging. A production promotion PR carries ONLY tickets sitting in this column, so a half-tested ticket cannot ride along with somebody else's release. Without it, promotion is all-or-nothing.

production.description: Only ever receives PRs from the integration branch.

integration.description: Where 'In review' work lives so a human can test it.

tests.description: One entry per suite. `command` is what both a human and CI run — prefer a make target or equivalent, never a raw tool invocation, so the two cannot drift apart.

integrationCommand.description: Optional slower suite needing real infrastructure.

glob.description: Used by test-inventory.sh to find test files.

language.description: Selects how test-inventory.sh extracts names and descriptions. `go` reads the `//` comment above `func TestX`; `vitest`/`jest` read the it()/test() string; `pytest` reads the docstring under `def test_x`; `rspec` reads the it() string. `other` lists files without extracting names.

lintCommand.description: Optional. Run alongside the suites before a review handoff.

ciCommand.description: Optional. The single target CI runs, if the project has one. review-handoff prefers this over running suites individually, because it is what actually gates the merge.

capabilities.description: Which installed skill provides each delegated job. `auto` means detect what is installed and ask once, then record the answer here. A concrete skill name is used without asking. `builtin` means use this plugin's own thinner version and stop offering alternatives. See references/capabilities.md in the plugin.

design-interview.description: Interrogates a feature idea until the user story is solid. Preferred: `grilling` (mattpocock-skills). Fallback: `superpowers:brainstorming`.

tdd-discipline.description: Owns test quality: seams, anti-patterns, vertical slices. Preferred: `tdd` (mattpocock-skills). Fallback: `superpowers:test-driven-development`. This plugin owns the red→green commit evidence regardless.

ticket-slicing.description: Breaks a large plan into tracer-bullet tickets with blocking edges. Preferred: `to-tickets` (mattpocock-skills).

code-review.description: Reviews a branch before handoff. Preferred: `code-review` (mattpocock-skills). Fallback: the built-in `/code-review` command.

ui-style.description: House design language for any new screen. There is no default — name your own, or omit it entirely. Skipped in silence when absent.

labels.description: Issue labels the workflow applies. Created on demand if missing.

verificationFailed.description: Applied when a human's manual check fails and the card is sent back from In review to In progress. The router treats a ticket carrying this label as a re-entry: read the failure comment before touching code.

environments.description: Where a human can go and try the work. Manual test steps reference these by name, and review-handoff refuses to write 'open dev' if it does not know where dev is.

taxonomy.description: How tickets are classified. Four dimensions kept separate, because collapsing them into one flat label list is how a tracker stops being able to answer basic questions. Omit this block entirely on a small project: tickets still work, they are just untyped.

typeLabels.description: Exactly one per ticket, never optional. Maps a kind of work to the label your tracker uses. A null value means the label does not exist yet: the skill puts the type in the title instead and says so, rather than filing a silently untyped ticket or inventing a label as a side effect. Suggested keys: bug, feature, task, security, docs, idea.

serviceLabels.description: Which service or component a ticket concerns. Inferred from the current repo's git remote, which removes the commonest source of mislabelling. Where the remote is not in the map, the skill ASKS rather than guessing.

prefix.description: Prepended to each value, so service labels sort together in the picker.

map.description: Repo name (as `gh repo view` reports it, without the owner) to service name. Two repos may map to one service.

areaLabels.description: Product areas. Zero or more per ticket, and they span services by design: a billing bug can touch three repos at once.

titlePrefix.description: Put `[service]` and, where the label is missing, `[type]` at the front of the title. Carries the classification even for dimensions that have no label yet.

priority.description: Priority belongs in a project FIELD, never a label — a label cannot be sorted on and invites one per ticket. Omit this block and priority is simply not set.

field.description: Name of the single-select project field.

default.description: Applied when nothing else decides. Make it a middle value. A default of the top level is how every ticket becomes top priority and the field stops carrying information.

levels.description: Level name to what it MEANS, in terms someone can disagree with. 'High' is not a definition; 'production down, data loss, or revenue blocked' is.

requireReasoning.description: The ticket body states why this level and not the one above or below. Makes the choice auditable, and gives a human something specific to argue with.

securityIsAlways.description: Level forced on anything typed security. Null to disable.

size.description: How much work, which is independent of how urgent. A one-line fix can be top priority and a three-week feature can be bottom. Omit to skip sizing.

anchors.description: Size to a concrete example from your own board. An anchor beats an adjective: 'comparable to #237' is checkable, 'medium' is not.

testers.description: People who sign off manual verification. Rendered as a named checkbox block on every ticket, so sign-off has an owner rather than being anonymous. Omit for a solo project.

diagrams.description: Mermaid renders natively in GitHub issues and PR bodies, so a diagram costs nothing to read and a great deal to leave out when a flow crosses a boundary.

validateWith.description: `mermaid-mcp` validates every diagram before it is posted. A broken fence renders as an error box that nobody notices until a reader hits it. `none` means open the issue and look.

requiredWhen.description: Situations where a diagram is not optional. Everything else is a judgement call, and the default answer is no diagram.

participantNames.description: Name participants the way the team talks about them (Portal, Backend, Stripe) rather than by class or function name.

style.description: House style for anything a person reads: tickets, PR bodies, UI copy, error messages.

emDashes.description: When forbidden, rewrite as two sentences. Applies inside diagram labels too.

extra.description: Any further house rules, one per line, applied to generated prose.

logging.description: What this project logs, how, and what it must never log. Recorded here so that logging is a DESIGN question answered while the ticket is written, rather than something remembered at review. ticket-authoring asks what a feature logs and at what level; red-green writes the call using `callPattern` rather than a bare console.log.

sink.description: Where logs end up so they can be queried after the fact: a hosted service, a file, a collector. Null means they stay on the console, which is a gap worth stating rather than a decision worth hiding.

callPattern.description: The exact call to write, verbatim, e.g. `this.logger.logInfo(message, context, meta)` or `log.info({ evt, ...meta })`. Skills copy this rather than inventing a logging idiom per file.

levels.description: Level to what it means HERE. Teams disagree about where INFO ends and DEBUG begins, so state it: e.g. DEBUG 'local diagnosis, off in production', INFO 'a thing happened that someone may later ask about', WARN 'recovered, but a human should know', ERROR 'the operation failed'.

logByDefault.description: Categories that get a log line as a matter of course, e.g. api-calls, user-actions, state-changes, errors, slow-requests. ticket-authoring turns these into design questions for any feature that touches them.

neverLog.description: Never written to a log at any level: tokens, passwords, full JWTs, API keys, session cookies, card details, anything from a credential file.

sanitisation.description: What is scrubbed automatically and what is not. Be honest about the gaps — 'the backend redacts known fields, the frontend redacts nothing' is the single most useful sentence in a logging policy, because it tells you where care is required.

apiConventions.description: The contract every endpoint in this project keeps. Decided once here so it is not re-litigated per endpoint, and so a ticket's design section can be checked against it.

errorShape.description: The JSON body of every error, as a literal example, e.g. `{"error": "...", "details": {"field": "..."}}`. One shape everywhere.

statusCodes.description: Situation to status, for the ones teams disagree on: validation failure, malformed body, not found, unauthorised, conflict.

internalErrorsLeak.description: When false, internal errors are logged in full and returned as a bare message with no detail — and there is a test asserting nothing leaks.

partialUpdate.description: How partial versus full update is expressed, e.g. 'PATCH with pointer fields so absent is distinguishable from set-to-zero; PUT with plain values'. If you have one you almost certainly want both, and a test for each.

listsAreNeverNull.description: An empty collection serialises as [] rather than null.

extra.description: Further conventions: pagination, versioning, idempotency, naming.

complexity.description: How hard the work is to reason about, which is NOT how much of it there is. A thousand-line rename is large and trivial; a twenty-line change to a concurrency invariant is small and hard. Size drives scheduling, complexity drives who or what should do it. Omit to skip the whole idea.

field.description: Project field name. Created by board-setup if absent.

levels.description: Level to what makes work land there. Describe the REASONING difficulty, not the line count: 'the change is obvious once located, one file, no design decisions' versus 'touches an invariant several callers depend on, and getting it wrong is silent'.

models.description: Which model should implement a ticket, chosen from its complexity. Recorded on the ticket so a session can switch before starting, and so a parallel fan-out does not send every sub-issue to the most expensive option. Omit and no model is ever suggested.

byComplexity.description: Complexity level to model name, e.g. {"trivial":"claude-haiku-4-5", "moderate":"claude-sonnet-5","hard":"claude-opus-5"}. Names must be ones the harness accepts; board-setup proposes current ones and the user corrects them.

default.description: Used when complexity is unset or unmapped. Prefer a mid tier.

escalateOn.description: Conditions that override the mapping upward regardless of complexity, e.g. security, data-migration, concurrency, auth. A cheap model on a cheap-looking auth change is the expensive mistake this prevents.

note.description: One line shown with the suggestion, e.g. 'switch with /model before starting'. The plugin records the choice; it does not switch the model itself.

epics.description: When a ticket is too big to be one ticket, it becomes a parent with GitHub sub-issues rather than a long checklist. Sub-issues carry a real parent link and GitHub tracks completion, so the epic cannot be signed off while a child is open.

label.description: Optional label applied to the parent, e.g. 'type:epic'. Null to rely on the sub-issue relationship alone.

splitWhen.description: Thresholds at which authoring proposes a split rather than one ticket. These are prompts for a conversation, never automatic.

criteriaAtLeast.description: Acceptance criteria count above which the work is probably several slices.

touchesServices.description: Number of services a single ticket spans before it wants splitting.

parallelisable.description: Record on each sub-issue whether it can start immediately or is blocked by a sibling. Independent children can be worked concurrently; dependent ones cannot, and saying which is which is the difference between a useful fan-out and a merge conflict.

provider.description: `auto`, `builtin`, or the exact name of an installed skill including any plugin prefix.

optional.description: When true, absence is skipped in silence rather than prompting.
